findings.claim: The pinned-object rule is contradicted by an explicit path fallback. If a recorded object is unavailable, reading the current pathname can reinterpret an existing run using different bytes; merely reporting an identity gap does not make eligibility, extraction, resume, or comparison trustworthy.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:73-79 permits path fallback for later readers, while :96-104 makes the pins part of verdict identity and requires cohort/scorecard agreement.
findings.fix: For identity-dependent operations, refuse when a pinned object is unavailable. Permit path fallback only for a clearly labeled non-authoritative diagnostic that cannot extract, grade, resume, or produce a verdict. Document how another machine fetches the recorded measuring commit or otherwise obtains the objects.

findings.claim: The proposal/compare specification still directs compare.py to current case and configuration paths, contradicting the global pinned-reader rule and leaving implementers a genuine choice about which bytes determine archived eligibility.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:73-79 says every later reader of a run reads case/configuration documents from caseTree/configTree; :211-219 instead says compare.py loads cases/<id>/<v>/case.json and configurations/<id>/<v>.json and justifies this through conventional immutability.
findings.fix: State explicitly in §7 that compare loads case.json from the run's caseTree and configuration JSON from its configTree, checks baseline/candidate pin equality before eligibility, and uses current paths only while authoring new proposals.

findings.claim: Committed in-place edits remain operationally possible under the same case version and instrument tag. The dirty check rejects only working-tree changes; after such an edit is committed, provisioning accepts a different caseTree but reuses the same caseId@caseVersion and tag, so the advertised immutability rule is not actually checked and tag publication can collide with an earlier instrument commit.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:44-59 calls case versions immutable but defines only a working-tree cleanliness refusal; :203-210 derives the tag solely from caseId and caseVersion; :303-312 acceptance tests only a dirty directory.
findings.fix: Make validate-kit reject changes to an existing case-version directory relative to its introduction commit, or define an authoritative append-only baseline/ledger. Add a fixture for a committed same-version edit and require refusal before creating or pushing the tag.

summary: All three round-5 findings are closed: provisioning and later readers are now nominally tied to pinned objects, alias-mode resume preserves legacy naming and identity for every repetition, and §10 names both cross-machine procedures. The projection and compatibility tables otherwise cover the shipped aliases; mission id taskrun fits current grammars and paths; explicit case/config versions are correctly mandatory for cohorts; raw-byte hashing avoids formatter and line-ending ambiguity, and the bounded tag fits Git ref constraints. Revision remains necessary because the path fallback and §7 current-path instruction undermine pinned identity, while committed same-version edits can still reuse an immutable semantic version and instrument tag.
